previews.label: 01 · ARRIVAL AND DIALOGUE
previews.title: Scene Club motion
previews.description: Aatami arrives, Jaska speaks, the authored decision is made, and the scene returns to Kallio. Includes bounded blink repairs.
previews.status: Review candidate · owner art approval pending

previews.label: 02 · AUTHORED CHAPTER
previews.title: Every encounter
previews.description: Browse all authored encounters with existing plates, choices and explicit placeholders for missing art or binding work.
previews.status: Playable review · authored text, proposed presentation

previews.label: 03 · THE CITY BETWEEN MOMENTS
previews.title: A quieter map
previews.description: Compare captured phone and desktop screens from the tested map cleanup, keeping travel and route decisions intact.
previews.status: Captured draft UI · map branch CI passed

previews.label: 04 · THE FIGHT STAYS C.19
previews.title: Combat evidence and UX
previews.description: Inspect all 15 measured fights and compare strategies, damage and police pressure. Proposal overlays keep the 3D battlefield.
previews.status: Measured bot data · UX overlays are proposals

previews.label: 05 · WHAT COMES HOME
previews.title: Consequences and recovery
previews.description: Try trade, hiring, loot, injuries, missing crew, arrests and recovery through isolated, labelled fixture states.

previews.label: 06 · THE TEN-DAY RUN
previews.title: Chapter and finale rehearsal
previews.description: Follow the actual schedule and mission dependencies. Explore the proposed shipment choice and 30% time budget before committing rules.
previews.status: Authored timeline · finale/time proposals not promoted

tasks.title: Record the three G0 routes on hardware
tasks.change: Use the existing door, getaway and Bear Path playtest links for a short device session.
tasks.acceptance: Record whether each fight made the player decide something, and any device failure, with actual device/browser details.
tasks.boundary: This remains owner/device acceptance. The preview pack and browser bots cannot sign it off.

tasks.title: Arrival into Scene Club
tasks.change: Integrate the reviewed arrival and return timing into the existing encounter shell after approval.
tasks.acceptance: Arrival, authored choice, saved result and return work in one loop at phone and desktop sizes.
tasks.boundary: New staging is a candidate. Do not promote semi-approved rigs or room by changing manifest labels.

tasks.title: Bounded eyelid repair
tasks.change: Replace rectangular eye swatches with reviewed eye-opening masks for Jaska and young Aatami front.
tasks.acceptance: Rest pixels remain unchanged; animated changes stay inside eye boxes and preserve glasses/brows.
tasks.boundary: The side rig is unassessed. Keep original sources and a rollback; new marker strokes need approval.
tasks.status: Review candidate and pixel checks ready

tasks.title: Readable landscape dialogue
tasks.change: Adapt the reviewed landscape composition while retaining the short bottom-tail bubble and source proportions.
tasks.acceptance: Dialogue is at least 12px, choices at least 44px, faces clear, with no clipped text at 844×390.
tasks.boundary: The current runtime landscape bubble is too small; passing choice tests alone is not readability acceptance.

tasks.title: Bind the six unillustrated encounters
tasks.change: Resolve their authored site/approach first, then preview existing bank, Harju and Jade-front plates where appropriate.
tasks.acceptance: Each binding matches the actual people and location; compare all affected scenes on phone and desktop.
tasks.boundary: First sale is outside the staffed bank. Courtyard Receipts is not Jaska’s room. Semi-approved plates remain candidates.

tasks.title: Source selection for missing contacts
tasks.change: Choose and document source references for Esa, Leena, Anne and Mei-Lan before extracting dedicated cut-ins.
tasks.acceptance: Each contact has a source identity, approval state, separable parts and real motion review.
tasks.boundary: Neutral placeholders are labels, not approved character designs. Do not generate replacements for existing approved identities.

tasks.title: Stakes before every consequential answer
tasks.change: Carry authored forecasts and blocking reasons through each encounter composition.
tasks.acceptance: All enabled choices show their stakes; unavailable choices explain why; reload cannot duplicate effects.
tasks.boundary: No invented odds or story branches. A battle choice goes to actual C.19 rather than a simulated result card.

tasks.title: Trim idle map repetition
tasks.change: Collapse identical location labels and show capacity guidance only while planning a route.
tasks.acceptance: Whole-state inspection invariance, route preview/cancel/pin and opening trade regressions pass.
tasks.boundary: Travel, route rules, current objective and pinned route controls remain intact.

tasks.title: One clear next action
tasks.change: Keep the persistent objective bar concise across travel, free blocks, encounters and unfinished fights.
tasks.acceptance: Exactly one primary next action is in view through the opening trade and after every return.
tasks.boundary: Do not hide optional exits, goals or actual costs merely to reduce text.

tasks.title: Explain a trip’s time commitment
tasks.change: Prototype a readable journey cost and resulting block/time before implementing D002.
tasks.acceptance: The chapter rehearsal exposes the effect of repeated travel; cancel/reload never charges a preview.
tasks.boundary: 30% of a block is an owner direction, but its chapter integration belongs at G4 and requires a complete-run test.

tasks.title: Local pressure where it matters
tasks.change: Show the relevant location’s pressure beside travel/door choices and their aftermath.
tasks.acceptance: The player can distinguish local pressure from the campaign clock and see a changed value after a result.
tasks.boundary: Pressure is not territory ownership; do not invent a corner-control feature.

tasks.title: Compact job commitment
tasks.change: Prototype a short door header with job, risk, pay and required crew before taking the block.
tasks.acceptance: All existing requirements and escalation forecasts remain available on a phone without duplicated exposition.
tasks.boundary: Do not drop late closing, fight caps, loss stakes or the choice to let a block pass.

tasks.title: Move, target and police forecasts together
tasks.change: Review overlays that explain movement, target validity and pressure in the actual 3D arena.
tasks.acceptance: A player can read the planned move/action and police timing before committing, at portrait and desktop sizes.
tasks.boundary: No replacement formation/card battle. No rules or source models change in an overlay study.

tasks.title: Measure defensive decisions
tasks.change: Instrument successful Brace/move/attack commands and compare attack-first with dodge-first.
tasks.acceptance: Saved deterministic samples show what each bot actually does; policy changes are separated from rule changes.
tasks.boundary: A bot choosing zero Braces is not proof that Brace is a bad player mechanic.

tasks.title: Reconcile planned and fallback enemy actions
tasks.change: Trace where a careful policy avoids announced danger but gets hit after an enemy presses around a block.
tasks.acceptance: One reproducible weak fight has per-command threats, fallback actions and resulting damage explained.
tasks.boundary: Investigate policy/model limits before tuning enemy damage or changing intent promises.

tasks.title: Make the carrier’s slower move readable
tasks.change: Expose the existing carrier restriction and the value of screening them near the exit.
tasks.acceptance: Actual C.19 getaway traces distinguish straight-out and escort choices, including costs.
tasks.boundary: Keep extraction, missing crew and loss prices intact; do not turn a getaway into a narrative dice card.

tasks.title: Track all 15 scenarios at 30 seeds
tasks.change: Compare outcome, damage, casualties, police and duration by scenario, heat and policy.
tasks.acceptance: Source JSON, seed count and policy identity are reproducible; unavailable metrics are shown as unmeasured.
tasks.boundary: Targets remain ROADMAP §5 proposals. No pooled average hides a broken mission.

tasks.title: Audit five arenas before geometry changes
tasks.change: Capture courtyard, yard, park, tram street and quay at their real camera angles and mark actual seams/occlusion.
tasks.acceptance: Before/after frames use matching cameras; cover, gates and floor transitions remain legible.
tasks.boundary: Use the existing kit incrementally. No speculative rebuilding or new model promotion.

tasks.title: Inspect gun targets without losing the board
tasks.change: Review the optional temporary shooter/target camera and a reliable return to planning view.
tasks.acceptance: The same target, costs, intent and return state are preserved through inspection and reduced motion.
tasks.boundary: A camera study does not authorize new combat rules or conceal the full board by default.

tasks.title: One result strip, paid once
tasks.change: Show money, loot, condition, missing/arrested crew and pressure at the place of return.
tasks.acceptance: Applying the same receipt again leaves the entire campaign unchanged; reload shows the same settled outcome.
tasks.boundary: Fixtures are review states, not measured victories. Preserve the existing campaign receipt path.

tasks.title: Show the promise with the hire
tasks.change: Put pay, availability and loyalty implications together before recruiting or accepting a short job.
tasks.acceptance: The selected authored hire changes the intended state once; the crew view explains what was promised.
tasks.boundary: Generated hires and authored runner choices are different sources and must be labelled.

tasks.title: Explain who can work next
tasks.change: Prototype distinct aftermath states for hurt, critical, missing and arrested crew.
tasks.acceptance: Names and existing condition/availability are readable; treatment/rescue/bail options show their actual requirements.
tasks.boundary: Do not invent recovery timers, resurrection rules or an unimplemented medical service.

tasks.title: A visible route home
tasks.change: Connect existing rescue doors and bail to the missing/arrested person and their cost.
tasks.acceptance: A real-engine fixture brings the intended person back without replaying payment or recovering unrelated crew.
tasks.boundary: Availability and time/cash costs come from the current model; a fixture is not a completed chapter run.

tasks.title: Show the actual chapter-income ledger
tasks.change: Compare fence, market-sale and route proceeds, then resolve the roadmap’s fence-only description against the current web model.
tasks.acceptance: Real API fixtures show which income paths increment chapterEarned; the intended eligible sources are recorded before any rule change.
tasks.boundary: ROADMAP describes fence money, but web state.js also counts transactOffer and sendOnRoute receipts. Do not silently force one interpretation or auto-sell gear.
tasks.status: Source mismatch exposed by real model fixtures

tasks.title: Remember the choice in the city
tasks.change: Surface an authored relationship, lead or pressure change on a return visit without repeating the whole result screen.
tasks.acceptance: The relevant memory survives reload and does not grant the reward again.
tasks.boundary: No new culprit, mission or faction plot is invented to fill a presentation gap.

tasks.title: Make the twenty-block spine inspectable
tasks.change: Lay out authored encounters, free blocks, missions and their dependencies in one rehearsal timeline.
tasks.acceptance: Every source encounter and schedule block is represented; unknown or optional paths remain explicit.
tasks.boundary: The atlas is a source index, not evidence that every declared effect executes.

tasks.title: Trace authored branches through ten days
tasks.change: Build deterministic policy runs that log choices, blocks, economy and reachability.
tasks.acceptance: All required story beats/endings stay reachable; each failed run identifies the exact blocked prerequisite.
tasks.boundary: Do not claim a full-run pass from isolated mission tests or a hand-written timeline.

tasks.title: Measure the €400 chapter-income gate
tasks.change: Rehearse the current shipment prerequisites and make the income-source mismatch visible.
tasks.acceptance: The tool names each actual blocked prerequisite and compares the current income ledger with the roadmap description.
tasks.boundary: The €400 income threshold and €400 cash stake are separate requirements. Do not lower either to make a fixture win; fence-only versus broader income needs source alignment.

tasks.title: Crew and route decision candidate
tasks.change: Prototype a shipment commitment with understandable tradeoffs using existing crew and authored destination.
tasks.acceptance: The owner can compare the current roll with a concrete crew/route proposal and see what remains unspecified.
tasks.boundary: New risk/reward numbers are placeholders; the choice-versus-played-fight question remains an owner decision.

tasks.title: Test 30%-of-block costs before G4
tasks.change: Compare current travel/trade time with the proposed budget, then run the actual chapter when implemented.
tasks.acceptance: Preview/cancel is free; one visit/trip charges once; ten-day runs verify content is still reachable.
tasks.boundary: A planning calculator is not the runtime D002 implementation or a measured complete-run result.

tasks.title: Preview what crosses the chapter boundary
tasks.change: Show current data-driven cash stake, stock reset, weapons and built network carryover.
tasks.acceptance: Exact carryover fixtures match chapter.js and reload cannot apply a second transition.
tasks.boundary: Chapter 2 content is not authored yet; do not fabricate its playable completion.

tasks.title: Device acceptance on real hardware
tasks.change: Collect physical Pixel/iPad observations for dialogue, touch targeting, motion and 3D arena performance.
tasks.acceptance: Owner/device evidence records what was actually played, device/browser and observed failures.
tasks.boundary: Browser emulation and SwiftShader are not physical-device acceptance.

tasks.title: Reload, interrupted graphics and saves
tasks.change: Reuse existing persistence/recovery suites for a run interrupted at every commitment/result boundary.
tasks.acceptance: No lost receipt, double reward, charged cancellation or permanent blank arena after recovery.
tasks.boundary: A schema or geometry check alone does not prove visual correctness.

tasks.title: A reviewable release candidate
tasks.change: Integrate approved slices, run relevant gates, then stage the hub with exact source/build receipts.
tasks.acceptance: Source SHA, hub SHA, version, CI and actual public playable route agree; rollback remains available.
tasks.boundary: No unapproved art promotion, silent deploy or completion percentage increase from code volume.

tasks.title: Keep source status visible
tasks.change: Maintain a per-scene/character inventory that separates registered files, source approval and runtime readiness.
tasks.acceptance: Every visible placeholder has a reason, source candidate and a defined next production gate.
tasks.boundary: Do not manufacture acceptance by relabelling a manifest entry.

tasks.title: A complete chapter verdict
tasks.change: Prepare a compact ten-day playtest with recorded decisions, rough edges and an owner verdict.
tasks.acceptance: At least one actual complete run and the required strategy/ending coverage are saved with reproducible evidence.
tasks.boundary: A checklist or preview gallery is preparation, not proof the chapter is fun or complete.
